scope: All customer behavior, fees, costs, bank delays, inventory and subscription consent are authored simulation assumptions.
No new PayPal API or Channel3 calls in this benchmark. Orders and supplier invoices are simulated; earlier Sandbox receipts remain separate.
The current catalogue is independently authored; no Channel3 product data is used.
The100-day campaign has a known endpoint. Inventory cover drops to7 days on day70; this needs separate testing before claiming year-round performance.
Aggregate gates do not establish that every counterparty benefits. Wholesaler and manufacturer losses are shown explicitly.
No2x claim, no production PayPal profit claim, no claim that additional agent roles have been causally validated.

Eight model calls total: six initial component designs, then two specialist revisions using measured development tool feedback. Four new revisions failed development promotion; the retained controller missed the aggregate partner-profit requirement on this new batch.
The failed first revision attempt exceeded the local input-size check before a provider call or reservation; it cost zero and is retained separately.

input.scope: Joint pricing, inventory and settlement policy. Prioritize actual customer value and viable supplier participation.
input.constraints: No private needs, preferences, wallets or future draws. No outcomes from the unopened validation markets are available. Numerical search alone produced1.7x on development but failed cash checks on another validation batch; that is a failure, not a winning policy. Inventory liquidation at the100-day boundary is not perpetual business growth.

options.rationale: Using learned policy with bank rails to avoid PayPal constraints, personalized marketing, and forest model for better predictions.
options.name: Learned-Bank-Forest

options.rationale: Using learned policy with auto rails, portfolio marketing, and extra_trees model with longer forecast window.
